schema.description: Attribution tree via each concept's `topic` field; `edges` holds only prereq edges.

node_fields.name: concept name
node_fields.topic: owning topic id; null for topic nodes
node_fields.default_order: default teaching order within the topic

edge_types.prereq: from must be learned before to; strength=hard|soft

nodes.name: Microscopy
nodes.description: The use of light and electron microscopes to view cells, where resolution—the ability to distinguish two close points—and magnification determine the detail observable.

nodes.name: Eukaryotic Organelles
nodes.description: Membrane-bound and non-membrane structures within eukaryotic cells, such as the nucleus, mitochondria, and endoplasmic reticulum, each performing specialised functions.

nodes.name: Prokaryotic Cells
nodes.description: Bacterial cells lacking a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, with circular DNA, smaller ribosomes, and a cell wall, contrasted with eukaryotic cells.

nodes.name: Cell Size and Magnification
nodes.description: Calculating actual cell size, magnification, and image size using the relationship that magnification equals image size divided by actual size, with consistent units.

nodes.name: Water
nodes.description: The properties of water arising from its polarity and hydrogen bonding, including its role as a solvent, high specific heat capacity, and cohesion important to life.

nodes.name: Carbohydrates
nodes.description: Sugars and polysaccharides built from monosaccharides via glycosidic bonds, including glucose, starch, glycogen, and cellulose, serving energy and structural roles.

nodes.name: Lipids
nodes.description: Hydrophobic molecules including triglycerides for energy storage and phospholipids whose amphipathic structure forms the bilayer of cell membranes.

nodes.name: Proteins
nodes.description: Polymers of amino acids joined by peptide bonds, folding through primary, secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structure that determines their biological function.

nodes.name: Biochemical Tests
nodes.description: Qualitative biochemical tests identifying biological molecules, such as Benedict's for reducing sugars, iodine for starch, biuret for protein, and the emulsion test for lipids.

nodes.name: Enzyme Action
nodes.description: Enzymes as biological catalysts lowering activation energy, binding substrates at their active site according to the induced-fit model to form products.

nodes.name: Factors Affecting Enzyme Activity
nodes.description: How temperature, pH, substrate concentration, and enzyme concentration affect the rate of enzyme-catalysed reactions, including denaturation at extremes.

nodes.name: Enzyme Inhibition
nodes.description: Reduction of enzyme activity by inhibitors, with competitive inhibitors binding the active site and non-competitive inhibitors binding elsewhere to alter it.

nodes.name: Membrane Structure
nodes.description: The fluid mosaic model describing the cell membrane as a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins, cholesterol, and glycoproteins controlling exchange.

nodes.name: Diffusion and Osmosis
nodes.description: Movement of substances down a concentration gradient without energy, by diffusion and facilitated diffusion, and the osmosis of water across membranes.

nodes.name: Active Transport
nodes.description: Movement of substances against a concentration gradient using ATP and carrier proteins, including bulk transport by endocytosis and exocytosis.

nodes.name: Chromosome Behaviour
nodes.description: The structure of chromosomes as DNA wound around histone proteins, and their replication and condensation in preparation for nuclear division.

nodes.name: Mitosis
nodes.description: Nuclear division producing two genetically identical daughter cells through prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase, underlying growth and repair.

nodes.name: DNA Structure
nodes.description: DNA as a double helix of two antiparallel nucleotide strands held together by complementary base pairing between adenine-thymine and guanine-cytosine.

nodes.name: DNA Replication
nodes.description: Semi-conservative replication in which the double helix unwinds and each strand templates a new complementary strand via DNA polymerase.

nodes.name: Transcription
nodes.description: The synthesis of a messenger RNA copy of a gene by RNA polymerase, using one DNA strand as a template in the nucleus.

nodes.name: Translation
nodes.description: The synthesis of a polypeptide at the ribosome, where transfer RNA matches anticodons to mRNA codons to assemble amino acids in sequence.

nodes.name: Gene Mutation
nodes.description: Changes to the DNA base sequence, such as substitutions, insertions, and deletions, which may alter the resulting protein and the phenotype.

nodes.name: Xylem and Water Transport
nodes.description: The transport of water and mineral ions upward through dead, lignified xylem vessels, driven by transpiration pull via the cohesion-tension mechanism.

nodes.name: Transpiration
nodes.description: The loss of water vapour from leaves through stomata, and the effect of light, temperature, humidity, and air movement on its rate.

nodes.name: Phloem and Translocation
nodes.description: The translocation of sucrose and other assimilates through living phloem sieve tubes from sources to sinks by pressure flow.

nodes.name: The Heart
nodes.description: The structure of the mammalian heart and the cardiac cycle of atrial and ventricular systole and diastole, coordinated to pump blood.

nodes.name: Blood Vessels
nodes.description: The structure and function of arteries, veins, and capillaries, whose walls suit carrying blood at different pressures and exchanging materials.

nodes.name: Haemoglobin and Oxygen Transport
nodes.description: Haemoglobin's reversible binding of oxygen described by the sigmoid dissociation curve, and the Bohr effect that shifts it with carbon dioxide.

nodes.name: Gas Exchange in the Lungs
nodes.description: Gas exchange in the alveoli, whose large, thin, moist surface and rich blood supply maximise diffusion of oxygen and carbon dioxide.

nodes.name: Infectious Disease
nodes.description: Diseases caused by pathogens such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, and protoctists, and the ways they are transmitted between hosts.

nodes.name: Immune Response
nodes.description: The body's defence against pathogens through phagocytes engulfing invaders and lymphocytes mounting specific cell-mediated and humoral responses.

nodes.name: Antibodies and Vaccination
nodes.description: Antibodies as proteins binding specific antigens to neutralise pathogens, and vaccination conferring active immunity through memory cells.

nodes.name: Glycolysis
nodes.description: The cytoplasmic breakdown of glucose into pyruvate, producing a small net yield of ATP and reduced NAD without requiring oxygen.

nodes.name: Link Reaction and Krebs Cycle
nodes.description: The link reaction converting pyruvate to acetyl coenzyme A, and the Krebs cycle oxidising it to release carbon dioxide and reduced coenzymes.

nodes.name: Oxidative Phosphorylation
nodes.description: Oxidative phosphorylation using the electron transport chain and chemiosmosis across the inner mitochondrial membrane to synthesise most ATP.

nodes.name: Anaerobic Respiration
nodes.description: Respiration without oxygen, regenerating NAD through lactate fermentation in animals or ethanol fermentation in yeast and plants, yielding little ATP.

nodes.name: Light-Dependent Reactions
nodes.description: The light-dependent reactions in the thylakoids capturing light to produce ATP and reduced NADP while splitting water to release oxygen.

nodes.name: Calvin Cycle
nodes.description: The Calvin cycle in the stroma fixing carbon dioxide using ATP and reduced NADP to synthesise carbohydrate via the enzyme RuBisCO.

nodes.name: Limiting Factors
nodes.description: Environmental factors such as light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, and temperature that limit the overall rate of photosynthesis.

nodes.name: Homeostasis Principles
nodes.description: The maintenance of a stable internal environment through negative feedback, where deviations from set points trigger corrective responses.

nodes.name: The Kidney and Osmoregulation
nodes.description: Ultrafiltration and selective reabsorption in the nephron forming urine, and the osmoregulation of water balance through the action of ADH.

nodes.name: Control of Blood Glucose
nodes.description: Regulation of blood glucose by insulin and glucagon from the pancreas, and the disruption of this control in diabetes mellitus.

nodes.name: Nervous Transmission
nodes.description: The transmission of nerve impulses as action potentials, generated by the movement of sodium and potassium ions across the neurone membrane.

nodes.name: Synapses
nodes.description: Chemical transmission across synapses, where neurotransmitter released from the presynaptic neurone diffuses to receptors on the postsynaptic membrane.

nodes.name: Hormonal Control
nodes.description: Endocrine coordination in which hormones secreted by glands travel in the blood to target cells, producing slower, longer-lasting responses.

nodes.name: Plant Responses
nodes.description: Plant responses to stimuli, including tropisms controlled by auxin and other growth regulators that direct growth toward or away from stimuli.

nodes.name: Meiosis
nodes.description: Reduction division producing four genetically varied haploid gametes, with crossing over and independent assortment generating genetic variation.

nodes.name: Genetic Crosses
nodes.description: Predicting inheritance using monohybrid and dihybrid crosses, applying dominance, codominance, and the characteristic ratios of Mendelian genetics.

nodes.name: Gene Linkage and Crossing Over
nodes.description: Genes on the same chromosome inherited together as linked genes, with crossing over producing recombinants at a frequency reflecting their distance.

nodes.name: Control of Gene Expression
nodes.description: The regulation of gene expression in eukaryotes, including transcriptional control and the role of regulatory proteins in switching genes on and off.

nodes.name: Variation
nodes.description: Genetic and environmental variation among individuals, with continuous and discontinuous variation arising from genes, environment, and their interaction.

nodes.name: Natural Selection
nodes.description: Differential survival and reproduction of individuals with advantageous alleles, changing allele frequencies in a population over generations.

nodes.name: Speciation
nodes.description: The formation of new species when populations become reproductively isolated, allowing them to diverge through allopatric or sympatric mechanisms.

nodes.name: Classification
nodes.description: The hierarchical classification of organisms into taxa and the three-domain system, reflecting their evolutionary relationships.

nodes.name: Biodiversity and Sampling
nodes.description: Measuring biodiversity using random sampling and indices such as Simpson's index to quantify species richness and evenness in a habitat.

nodes.name: Conservation
nodes.description: Methods of maintaining biodiversity and ecosystems, balancing human activity with the protection of species and their habitats.

nodes.name: Gene Technology
nodes.description: Recombinant DNA technology cutting and joining DNA with enzymes to insert genes into vectors, enabling gene cloning and expression.

nodes.name: PCR and Electrophoresis
nodes.description: The polymerase chain reaction amplifying DNA in vitro, and gel electrophoresis separating DNA fragments by size for analysis.

nodes.name: Applications of Genetic Technology
nodes.description: Applications of genetic technology in medicine and agriculture, including genetically modified organisms, gene therapy, and genetic screening.
